_readme: What a release APK is allowed to weigh, read by scripts/perf/apk-size.mjs.
Keyed by ABI set, because an all-four-ABI build is roughly three times an
arm64-only one and comparing the two is noise rather than a regression.
The numbers below were measured from the v0.28.0 release asset. The first
baseline came from v0.14.1, the first build carrying both minification
flags: 3 dex files rather than the 6 an unminified build produces, and lib/
deflated rather than STORED. Anything that undoes either shows up here as
tens of percent, not as noise. v0.29.0 added pdf-lib and fontkit for the
training report, about 1.4 MB of bundle, measured at 32.75 MB in CI.
v0.31.0 added the food tracker: expo-camera with its on-device barcode reader
(native lib, model asset and a fourth dex file), expo-image-picker and
expo-image-manipulator, and the food screens. Recorded from the CI log of the
v0.31.0 build, which this gate stopped before upload, so it was not installed.
tolerancePercent is headroom for a feature release, not a target. Raise it
only with the reason in the commit message. To move a baseline, run
'node scripts/perf/apk-size.mjs <apk> --update' against a build you have
installed and opened, and commit the result alongside the change that grew
it, so the diff says what bought the megabytes.
